title: Associations Between Adherence to the 24-Hour Movement Guidelines and Mental Health Outcomes in Adolescents: The Mediating Role of Weight Status
content: Background: Recent evidence supports the hypothesis that adherence to the 24-Hour Movement Guidelines (24-HMG) is associated with both mental health and weight status, while excess body weight plays an important role in youth mental health. Accordingly, weight status may mediate the association between adherence to the 24-HMG and mental health outcomes, particularly depressive, anxiety, and stress symptoms. Objective: To identify associations between adherence to the 24-HMG and mental health outcomes among basic education students and subsequently explore the mediating role of weight status in these associations. Methods: This school-based observational study included 1,022 students aged 11-19 years (mean age, 14.9 ± 2.5 years; 51.5% girls). A structured questionnaire was administered to assess physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep duration. Mental health outcomes were assessed using the DASS-21. Weight status was determined based on body mass index. Structural equation modeling was used to examine direct and indirect pathways, adjusting for relevant covariates. Results: Path analysis showed that weight status was positively associated with depressive symptoms (β = 0.196 [95% CI 0.117 to 0.288]; p = 0.023), anxiety symptoms (β = 0.179 [95% CI 0.108 to 0.263]; p = 0.028), and stress symptoms (β = 0.147 [95% CI 0.079 to 0.228]; p = 0.041), indicating that students with overweight or obesity tended to have poorer mental health. Similarly, the number of 24-HMG met was inversely associated with depressive symptoms (β = −0.319 [95% CI −0.448 to −0.177]; p < 0.001), anxiety symptoms (β = −0.278 [95% CI −0.391 to −0.153]; p = 0.001), and stress symptoms (β = −0.251 [95% CI, −0.353 to −0.131]; p = 0.012), suggesting that meeting a greater number of healthy movement behavior guidelines was associated with lower levels of psychological distress. In addition, a mediating role of weight status was observed in the associations between adherence to the 24-HMG and depressive symptoms (β = 0.006 [95% CI 0.004 to 0.010]) and anxiety symptoms (β = 0.004 [95% CI 0.002 to 0.007]). Conclusion: The findings indicate that students who met a greater number of the 24-HMG reported better mental health outcomes. Although weight status was independently associated with depressive, anxiety, and stress symptoms, its mediating role was limited, suggesting that other unmeasured mediators may have played a more substantial role.
